title: Ishan Kishan, Tilak Varma Power India to T20 Series Win in Zimbabwe
excerpt: Kishan's 81 off 44 balls and Varma's unbeaten 60 propelled India to 219/5 before bowling Zimbabwe out for 129, securing a 2-0 series lead in Harare.
body:
• Ishan Kishan smashed 81 off 44 balls and Tilak Varma hit an unbeaten 60 off 29 as India posted 219/5 in the second T20I at Harare Sports Club.
  • Zimbabwe were bowled out for 129, handing India a 90-run victory and an unassailable 2-0 series lead.
  • Abhishek Sharma took 3-17 with his left-arm spin, while debutant Yash Thakur impressed with 2-30.
  • Fast bowler Prince Yadav left the field with a hamstring injury after bowling just 1.2 overs — a concern for India's pace reserves.

India crushed Zimbabwe by 90 runs in the second T20 international at Harare Sports Club on Saturday, clinching the three-match series 2-0 with a dominant all-round display. Ishan Kishan's explosive 81 off 44 balls and vice-captain Tilak Varma's unbeaten 60 off 29 deliveries powered a total of 219/5, before India's bowlers dismissed the hosts for 129 in 17.5 overs.

The result also marked Shreyas Iyer's first series win since taking over as India's T20I captain. Iyer had won his previous eight tosses but lost six of those matches in Ireland and England. On Saturday he finally lost a toss — and his team delivered their most convincing performance of his tenure, according to Cricbuzz.

Kishan and Varma Rescue India After Early Wobble

Zimbabwe won the toss and inserted India, and the decision initially paid off. Blessing Muzarabani removed opener Abhishek Sharma for eight with extra bounce from a back-of-a-length delivery. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi counter-attacked with three fours and a six off Richard Ngarava in the third over, but his 20 off nine balls ended when Ngarava bounced him out — the teenager skied a sharp short ball to mid-on.

At 29/2, India were in trouble. Kishan and captain Iyer steadied the innings with a 66-run partnership for the third wicket, mixing caution with aggression on a surface where the ball was not coming on easily. Iyer struck three boundaries off Brian Bennett in the 10th over before falling off the last ball for 25.

That brought Varma to the crease, and the fourth-wicket pair shifted into overdrive. Kishan and Varma put on 94 off just 44 balls, according to Reuters, dismantling bowling that strayed too full. Kishan employed the pull shot to perfection — 46 of his 81 runs came through mid-wicket and long-on — and slogged Sikandar Raza for a six before he was caught at deep point in the 18th over.

"Batting in the middle overs was very challenging."

— Tilak Varma, India vice-captain, to host broadcaster

Varma, who had faced scrutiny over his ability to accelerate in the middle overs against spin, answered his critics with a blistering knock — five fours and three sixes — that carried India past 210. Rinku Singh and Shivam Dube added late blows to push the total to 219/5.

Zimbabwe Collapse After Bennett's Brief Resistance

Chasing a record target, Zimbabwe opener Brian Bennett attacked from the start, using the scoop shot effectively against Mayank Yadav and debutant Yash Thakur. Bennett's 32 off 19 balls offered early hope, but he was cramped for room attempting a reverse scoop off Thakur and lobbed the ball to the wicketkeeper.

That dismissal triggered a rapid collapse. Prince Yadav and Ravi Bishnoi reduced Zimbabwe to 49/4 shortly after the powerplay, and the hosts slumped to 65/5 in the ninth over. Abhishek Sharma's left-arm spin proved decisive — three wickets for 17 runs hastened the end as Zimbabwe were bowled out in the 18th over.

Injury Cloud Over Prince Yadav

The one blemish on India's afternoon was the injury to Prince Yadav. The young pacer hobbled off clutching his left hamstring after bowling just 1.2 overs, despite having already claimed figures of 2-10. His fitness will be monitored ahead of Sunday's finale. Thakur, playing his first T20I, filled the void capably with 2-30 in four overs.

Series Sealed, Dead Rubber on Sunday

India won the opening match by seven wickets with 40 balls to spare, and Saturday's hammering underscored the gulf between the sides. For Indian cricket fans following from abroad, the series has showcased emerging talent — Sooryavanshi's fearless hitting, Thakur's composed debut, and Kishan's return to top form. The third and final T20I takes place at the same venue on Sunday, with India eyeing a clean sweep.

Brief Scores: India 219/5 in 20 overs (Ishan Kishan 81, Tilak Varma 60*; Newman Nyamhuri 1-25) beat Zimbabwe 129 all out in 17.5 overs (Brian Bennett 32; Abhishek Sharma 3-17, Prince Yadav 2-10, Yash Thakur 2-30) by 90 runs.
nri_angle: The emphatic series win gives Indian cricket fans abroad a weekend highlight, with Shreyas Iyer's young squad showing depth and firepower ahead of a packed international calendar.
